# Lunosia

> A free Spanish trainer built around speaking. You hold a conversation out
> loud with a partner that stays in character; when you get something wrong it
> tells you what to say instead and names the rule you broke, then brings that
> sentence back days later until you can produce the fix from memory. No
> account, no subscription, no paid tier, and it works offline after the first
> visit.

Lunosia covers six skills: speaking (23 scenarios), listening, reading (12
graded stories, every word one tap from its meaning), writing (24 tasks, each
checked), pronunciation (10 sounds English speakers get wrong by reflex) and
grammar (20 lessons aimed at the points where English actively misleads you).

The grammar checker is a rules engine rather than a language model. It knows
the gender of eighteen thousand nouns and the person of any verb form, so
where it speaks it is not guessing, and it can name the rule it applied —
which is what turns a correction into a lesson. It is measured at zero false
positives across more than eight hundred sentences of known-good Spanish,
because a learner told their correct sentence was wrong learns something false
and stops trusting the tool.

It costs nothing to use and nothing to run: the dictionary is built from open
data, the grammar and pronunciation engines run in the reader's own browser,
and the conversation partner runs on free infrastructure. There is no paid
tier to upgrade to.

Speaking needs Chrome, Edge, Safari or Samsung Internet — Firefox has never
implemented speech recognition. Everything else, including the full
conversation by typing, works in any current browser.

## Guides

- [Spanish for English speakers](https://lunosia.com/guides/): the twenty points where Spanish and English disagree hard enough that an English speaker gets them wrong by default.
- [ser, estar, tener and hay](https://lunosia.com/guides/ser-estar.html): four ways Spanish says what English says with "to be" and "to have".
- [Gender, agreement and word order](https://lunosia.com/guides/gender-and-agreement.html): why "la problema" and "un rojo coche" mark you out.
- [Verbs that do not behave like English](https://lunosia.com/guides/verbs-that-differ.html): gustar runs backwards, the ending is the pronoun, two verbs mean "to know".
- [The past tenses, por vs para, and the subjunctive](https://lunosia.com/guides/past-and-subjunctive.html): the four things that separate getting by from being fluent.
- [The small words that give you away](https://lunosia.com/guides/small-words.html): double negatives, muy against mucho, accents, and words that lie.
- [Spanish pronunciation](https://lunosia.com/guides/pronunciation.html): ten sounds, what your mouth does instead, and how to fix each one.

## About the site

- [About Lunosia](https://lunosia.com/about.html): what it is for and how the corrections work.
- [Privacy](https://lunosia.com/privacy.html): everything is stored in your own browser; the one thing that leaves your device is your side of a conversation.
- [Terms](https://lunosia.com/terms.html)
- [Contact](https://lunosia.com/contact.html)
